title: What if electrons disappeared for 5 seconds? You're in Central Park when every electron on Earth vanishes. The sky turns black at noon. Light passes straight through everything, even your hands. Every atom becomes pure positive charge, and positive charges repel. One grain of sand releases the energy of a 10-megaton bomb. Every person outshines the Sun. Earth comes apart at nearly the speed of light. When the electrons come back, there's nothing left to come back to. Which one next? 👇 #whatif #pov #simulation #science #physics
audio: NO voiceover. faster-whisper small (CPU) returned zero speech segments. Soundtrack is music + sound design: bright park ambience 0-7 s (~-23 dB), a big impact hit at 8 s (-12 dB) when electrons vanish, then a muffled low drone 9-27 s (spectral centroid drops from ~2 kHz to ~300-500 Hz, i.e. sound 'goes underwater'), accent hits at 19 s and 30 s, a rising bright hiss 31-41 s (centroid ~4.5 kHz) building to the whiteout peak at 41-42 s, a sustained loud rumble 43-65 s, a second hit at 69 s (second explosion), then fade to near-silence over the end card 72-80 s. Sound tracks the physics: when electrons go, the audio loses its highs.
transcript_source: burned-in captions read visually (2 fps crops); see research/library/transcripts/7693494009494342945.txt
title_pattern: 'What if [fundamental thing] disappeared for [N] seconds?' + second-person POV setup ('You're in Central Park when ...') + escalating consequence chain in the description + 'Which one next? 👇' comment bait + #whatif #pov #simulation. The caption is literally the whole script (every on-screen line, slightly expanded), so silent readers get the story before pressing play. Formula: tiny cause (a few seconds, one particle) -> planet-scale effect. The short, exact duration ('5 seconds') makes it feel testable and finite, and the familiar named location grounds the absurd premise.

thumbnail.composition: TikTok cover = frame 0. Full-bleed 9:16 low-poly 3D render of Central Park on a sunny afternoon: green lawn fills the lower 55%, a dark band of low-poly trees across the middle, Manhattan towers against a pale sky across the top. Foreground left-centre: three blocky low-poly people sitting on a red/white checkered picnic blanket, seen from slightly above and behind. A glowing 3D atom icon (red/white nucleus with a '+', blue electron orbits labelled e-) floats top-centre, with the two-line title directly under it. Top-left of the lawn holds a small HUD: 'ELECTRONS DISAPPEAR IN / 0:08.000 / EVERY ATOM ON EARTH HAS THEM'.
thumbnail.text: 'What if electrons disappeared for 5 seconds?' in a light serif (book-style, not a bold sans), white, two lines centred at ~25% height, about 5% of frame height per line; only the word 'electrons' tinted pale blue to match the atom's electron glow. HUD in small tracked-out uppercase sans with a large thin serif digital timer.
thumbnail.colours: Saturated grass green and red/white checker in the lower half; desaturated grey-blue sky and towers; pale blue accent on 'electrons' and the electron orbs; white text. The palette is calm and everyday, the 'before' state.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: A small glowing atom placed above an entire city skyline and park full of people: the subatomic thing set against the human/city scale. The picnic people are small, the skyline huge, and the atom is drawn bigger than a skyscraper.
thumbnail.why_it_works: It reads as a calm, ordinary scene with a ticking countdown, which promises that something is about to happen to it. The question is fully legible, the one coloured keyword tells you what the video is about in a glance, and the atom icon adds 'science' credibility. The serif type and soft render look like a premium simulation rather than meme content. The countdown already running on the cover is a built-in reason to stay and watch.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [on-screen, no VO] What if electrons disappeared for 5 seconds?  |  HUD: ELECTRONS DISAPPEAR IN 0:08.000 ... 0:03.533 / EVERY ATOM ON EARTH HAS THEM  |  at 5.0 s: You're in Central Park, New York.
hook.device: Countdown-to-catastrophe: a live millisecond timer ('ELECTRONS DISAPPEAR IN 0:08.000') counts down in real time from frame 0 over a peaceful everyday scene, so the viewer is locked in until zero. It is paired with the question title, a second-person POV location anchor at 5 s ('You're in Central Park'), and a calm 'before' world (ambient park sound, dog running, picnic) that the viewer knows is about to be destroyed. The payoff lands exactly at 8.0 s with a hard cut and an audio hit.

beats.summary: Title question over the calm low-poly Central Park picnic scene with a glowing atom icon; HUD countdown 'ELECTRONS DISAPPEAR IN 0:08' already running; sub-label 'EVERY ATOM ON EARTH HAS THEM'.
Title fades; 'You're in Central Park, New York.' Camera drifts across the lawn (dog running, people strolling); the atom icon shrinks into the HUD; the timer hits zero.

Hard cut with an impact sound: the sky goes black at noon and the whole world becomes see-through white edge-lines (X-ray/wireframe). HUD flips to 'ELECTRONS RETURN IN 0:05.000 / TIME SLOWED DOWN 11x'. 'Light now passes straight through everything.' The Sun becomes a white flare star in a black sky.
Wide wireframe skyline with a dog frozen mid-leap (slowed time), then the camera tilts down to the dark star-speckled ground. No caption: a breather for looking.
First-person POV: your own translucent wireframe hands raised, stars visible through them. 'You can see the stars through your hands.'
Two-step physics setup over wireframe people in the park: 'Every atom is now pure positive charge.' then 'And positive charges repel.' Low drone and slow camera moves: tension builds.
Camera tilts down; sand grains start to sparkle like stars, then back to the POV hands, which glow brighter and brighter. 'Each grain of sand becomes a nuclear bomb.' Rising hiss in the audio.
Tilt up to the park: people become blinding white silhouettes and the skyline blooms. 'Each person outshines the Sun.' The image blows out to pure white at ~41 s (audio peak).

Pull-out reveals Earth as a glowing white sphere with swirling blue plasma texture. 'Earth comes apart at nearly light speed.' HUD sub-label 'EARTH IS NOW 37,873 MILES WIDE' climbs continuously. The dark Moon passes in front as the sphere grows past the frame. 'More than the Milky Way will ever shine.'

Reframe to the expanding Earth's limb rising toward a cratered Moon; the limb swallows the Moon at ~55 s. HUD: 'THE MOON IS GONE'. Long uncaptioned stretch of churning cloud-plasma while the return timer runs down to 0:00.047. Sustained rumble.

White flash, then hard cut to Central Park rebuilt as a sparse blue point cloud. HUD 'ELECTRONS BACK / CENTRAL PARK, 5 SECONDS LATER'. 'Every electron returns to where it was.' Then the particles streak upward and blow apart against a blue sky: 'With nothing to hold them, they explode too.' / 'SAME ENERGY AS THE FIRST BLAST'. The return makes things worse.

Dark charcoal end card repeating the title (with 'electrons' in blue) plus a small monospace fact line: 'ELECTRONS ARE 0.03% OF YOUR MASS AND EVERY CHEMICAL BOND IN YOUR BODY'. Near-silent hold that suits a loop or a rewatch.

pacing.caption_interval_s: a new caption every ~4-6 s from 5 s to 53 s, then a 12 s uncaptioned stretch (53-65 s) carried by the visuals + HUD sub-labels, then 2 captions in 6 s for the twist
pacing.avg_shot_length_note: Only 3 hard cuts (4 'worlds': normal park / wireframe park / planet / point-cloud park). Within each world it plays as one continuous virtual camera with whip-tilts and blur-pans, so visual changes happen every ~3.3 s (24 shots / 80 s) and there are no edits.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: about 4-5 s: each caption is one bigger consequence, and the HUD timer is always moving, which acts as a constant progress bar
pacing.escalation_ladder: hands (you) -> sand grain -> people -> Earth -> Moon -> Milky Way comparison -> twist (the return is also catastrophic)

techniques_worth_copying: On-screen countdown HUD as the spine of the video: 'X DISAPPEARS IN 0:08.000' counting in milliseconds, then 'X RETURNS IN 0:05.000' running 11x slower with a 'TIME SLOWED DOWN 11x' label. This turns a 5-second premise into an 80-second video, gives a constant progress bar, and the viewer always knows when the payoff is.
HUD sub-label used as a second narration channel for hard numbers ('EARTH IS NOW 387,152 MILES WIDE' ticking up live, 'THE MOON IS GONE'), so the main caption stays short and poetic.
No voiceover: one short italic serif sentence per beat, centred low (~67% height). It works muted and translates to any language, and the description repeats the full script for silent readers.

Second-person POV anchored in a famous, ordinary place ('You're in Central Park'), plus first-person shots of 'your hands' at two key moments (seeing through them, then them glowing) to make the physics personal.

Visual-state change as the payoff, not a cutaway: the same scene re-rendered in a new material (normal -> X-ray wireframe -> glowing -> point cloud), so the viewer sees the world change rather than being told.
Strict escalation ladder of scale: you -> sand -> people -> Earth -> Moon -> galaxy comparison, with each caption one notch bigger.
Two-sentence mechanism ('Every atom is now pure positive charge.' / 'And positive charges repel.') placed before the escalation, so the destruction feels earned and logical.
Twist ending that inverts the expected reset: the electrons coming back doesn't save anything ('they explode too').
Sound design that follows the physics: highs drop out when the electrons vanish (muffled drone), a rising hiss into the whiteout, and silence on the end card.
Exposure blowout to pure white as the transition between scales (city -> planet).
End card repeats the title with one keyword in an accent colour, plus a surprising fact line (0.03% of your mass): a loop/rewatch prompt and comment fuel ('Which one next?').

Consistent typography system: light serif for the title/captions, tracked-out uppercase sans for HUD labels, thin serif tabular digits for the timer, and a soft dark blur behind the HUD/captions so they stay legible on white frames.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Feasible in Remotion with @remotion/three (Three.js is code, not AI video) or as a simplified 2.5D SVG/Canvas version. The look depends on 4 render 'materials' applied to one low-poly scene, a HUD component, and good bloom.
scene_assets: Procedural low-poly park: plane with grass gradient, instanced cone/icosahedron trees, box-extrusion skyline (random heights, window-grid texture via shader or canvas), blocky box-people (torso/head/limbs from boxes), checkered blanket plane, a box dog with a leap pose.
POV hands: two blocky hand meshes (palm box + 4-5 finger boxes) parented to the camera.
Planet: sphere with an animated fbm-noise shader (white/pale blue swirls) + fresnel rim glow; Moon sphere with a crater noise texture; a starfield (Points).
materials_states: Normal: flat-shaded colour + soft shadows, pale sky.
X-ray/wireframe: black background, EdgesGeometry lines in pale blue-white + faint transparent fills; ground as a dense random speck field.
Glowing: emissive white materials ramping up + UnrealBloomPass (or a CSS/canvas blur-add pass) to blow out to white.
Point cloud: sample points on mesh surfaces (MeshSurfaceSampler) rendered as small blue Points on navy, then animate them upward with velocity streaks for the explosion.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Scripted keyframed camera path per beat: slow trucks, fast whip-tilts with motion blur (render with @remotion/motion-blur or accumulation of 4-8 sub-frames), crane down, POV sway (low-amplitude noise), planet pull-back.
overlays: HUD component: label 'ELECTRONS DISAPPEAR IN' / 'ELECTRONS RETURN IN' / 'ELECTRONS BACK', tabular-figure timer driven by frame (with a time-scale factor of 11), animated sub-label with a counting number, soft dark radial blur behind it for legibility.
Caption component: centred italic serif (e.g. EB Garamond/Cormorant Italic), white with a soft shadow, 0.3 s fade in/out, one line per beat.
Title card with an inline keyword accent colour + a 3D or SVG atom icon (nucleus + 3 rotated ellipse orbits with glowing orbiting dots).
End card: charcoal background, title + monospace fact line.
code_only_remake_needs.transitions: Hard cut with a single bright flash frame at the vanish moment, exposure-to-white dissolve between scales, white flash on the return.
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Royalty-free/procedural ambience + impact hits + low-pass filter automation (cut highs after the vanish), riser into the whiteout, rumble bed, silence on the end card. No VO needed (optional Kokoro VO would change the format).
code_only_remake_needs.svg_2d_fallback: If Three.js is too heavy: parallax layered SVG skyline/trees/people; swap fill to stroke-only for the X-ray state; a canvas particle layer for sand sparkles and the point cloud; a canvas noise-sphere (or pre-baked shader in WebGL canvas) for the planet; CSS blur+brightness for bloom. Loses the true 3D camera moves but keeps the HUD/caption/escalation structure that carries most of the retention.
code_only_remake_needs.render_cost: 80 s at 1080x1920 30 fps = 2400 frames; bloom + motion blur sub-frames are the expensive part; on the Spark CPU (Remotion --concurrency=4) budget roughly 30-60 min per render. Use a lower sub-frame count for drafts.
